lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Make sure the LinkedIn or portfolio link points to a complete, current profile.
Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not generally needed on a US resume and could invite bias.

items.says: Include nationality only if it is relevant, and state work authorization directly if that is the concern.
items.because: Nationality does not directly establish work authorization.

items.says: Consider adding GPA, honors, or relevant coursework if accurate and helpful.
items.because: Some target roles screen for them.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration does not establish an interest-rate hedge.
items.because: It generally adds fixed-rate exposure; the risk being offset and hedge mechanics are not explained.

items.says: Define the sample and comparison behind the approval-rate change.
items.because: The number of applications reviewed and the meaning of “early defaults” are unclear.

items.says: Make clear that the change from 41% to 48% is seven percentage points.
Substantiate the link between the analysis and the approval-rate increase.
items.because: The bullet implies the analysis caused the outcome.

items.says: Change the present-tense verb to match the past-tense role.
items.because: It clashes with the role dates and surrounding bullets.

items.says: Clarify the period and scope of the reduction in missed covenant tests.
Say how often the template was used or how many memos it affected, if verifiable.
items.because: That would show the scale of the improvement.

items.says: Define the forecast-error measure and period, including whether the result is monthly or aggregate.
items.because: “Under 4%” is unclear.

items.says: Clarify what USD 600M represents.
items.because: The scale is otherwise hard to assess.

items.says: Explain how the forecast informed the USD 40M debt paydown.
items.because: The attribution is otherwise hard to assess.

items.says: Specify what the eight-to-five-working-day measure refers to.
Name the tools or systems that enabled the automation, if accurate.
items.because: Employers could better judge its relevance to their environment.

items.says: Clarify whether the shared discount rate and payback rules were approved policy or a modeling convention, and how project risk was handled.
items.because: A single rate may not suit projects with different risk profiles.

items.says: Describe the standardization’s effect on decisions or workflow.
items.because: The bullet currently describes standardization but not its effect.

items.says: Make the opening verb’s tense consistent with the completed experience.
items.because: It is in the present progressive.

items.says: Clarify when the mapping and reduction happened.
Define what “manual journal entries” counts.
Say whether the reduction in manual journal entries was sustained.
The FCFE and WACC valuation methods are mismatched.
items.because: FCFE is normally discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is normally used with free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: Use this space for a higher-impact result if training or documentation is not relevant to the target role.
items.because: This bullet has less impact than the quantified accomplishments above.

items.says: State the valuation date and how the market-price comparison was made.
Explain the assumptions and comparable-company check rather than treating proximity to market price as forecast quality.
items.because: Being within 6% of market price does not, by itself, establish forecast quality.

items.says: The stated 25% decline from USD 50 to USD 40 is incorrect.
items.because: That decline is 20%.

items.says: Define forecast accuracy and its baseline.
Clarify whether the change from 70% to 82% is 12 percentage points or a 12% relative improvement.
Explain the evaluation period and method behind “across 10 years.”
items.because: Readers may interpret it as testing a long-term forecast against actual results; an accuracy-improvement claim needs a defensible backtest or comparable evidence.

items.says: Clarify whether the work was FP&A support or fund analysis and reporting.
items.because: The FP&A-team wording appears inconsistent with the Student Investment Fund role and raises questions about ownership.

items.says: Explain what changed in the report and identify the benchmark and period.
Identify the committee’s role and substantiate its use of the report at every meeting.
Prioritize evidence of analytical work if the notes were not used by later analysts or space is limited.
Specify your Excel level and demonstrable capabilities.
items.because: “Excel” alone is too broad for finance roles.

items.says: Add other tools only if you have genuinely used them.
Align the methods list with target roles and be ready to give a concrete example of each.
items.because: The listed methods are general.

items.says: Update current status or activities if needed.
items.because: The latest employment entry ends in June 2025, so the timeline should be current.

items.says: Put the strongest, most relevant results first within each role.
items.because: Readers should see the fit before process details.
